chunks: Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, raising it, said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Rasool Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Teach your children swimming and archery.'
ai.seo_question: What skills should parents teach their children according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi’s chapter on child discipline, this hadith establishes swimming and archery as essential physical competencies for Muslim youth, reflecting the Prophetic emphasis on holistic development that combines spiritual, intellectual, and martial readiness. In Shia scholarly tradition, these skills are viewed not merely as recreational activities but as vital preparations for defense and self-reliance, ensuring the community remains capable and resilient.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, raising it, said,
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Teach your children swimming and the archery’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Asbat has narrated from his uncle Ya’qub ibn Salim in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You should teach your children swimming and sharp shooting.’”
